title: PSG14: isolated root records with adaptive inverse-cubic tolerance

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG14 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 against every adaptive adversary in the exact error model of the fifth claim with malformed fraction at most epsilon(n)=1/(1073741824 n^3), including the clean-input adversary. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s)=O(n^4 (log2 n)^(3/2) 2^(n/6)). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n)=n^4 (log2 n)^(3/2) 2^(n/6), for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 1. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and fractional-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG14 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 against every adaptive adversary in the exact error model of the fifth claim with malformed fraction at most epsilon(n)=1/(1073741824 n^3), including the clean-input adversary. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its peak classical bits obeys S_C(N,s)=O(n^2). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_C(n)=n^2, for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and fractional-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG14 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 against every adaptive adversary in the exact error model of the fifth claim with malformed fraction at most epsilon(n)=1/(1073741824 n^3), including the clean-input adversary. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its peak qubits obeys S_Q(N,s)=O(n). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_Q(n)=n, for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and fractional-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG14 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 against every adaptive adversary in the exact error model of the fifth claim with malformed fraction at most epsilon(n)=1/(1073741824 n^3), including the clean-input adversary. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its total acquired source copies, including all failed and discarded copies obeys Q(N,s)=O(n^4). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_Q(n)=n^4, for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and fractional-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N>=2, every s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), and every adaptive adversary of the exact structured error model, the single PSG14 algorithm and all parameter rules of proof.md tolerate malformed fraction epsilon(n)=1/(1073741824 n^3) with no validity threshold. Its acquisition count is exactly Q=2^40 n^4 on every branch, so at most floor(epsilon(n)Q)=1024n copies may be malformed. It returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. The adversary that corrupts nothing is included. This is a guaranteed fractional tolerance, not a per-copy corruption probability or a claim of maximal tolerance.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
